name: skyscanner-scraper (omkarcloud)
what_it_holds: Actively maintained (updated 2026-09-08) scraper/API wrapper claiming to pull Skyscanner flight search results as structured JSON (routes, prices, dates); free tier of 1,000 calls/month advertised. No historical data committed, method only.
why_useful: Another non-Airbnb, actively maintained flight-search puller relevant to gap 10 (airline capacity/traffic) and general travel-demand cross-checks; scraping Skyscanner is outside the sanctioned-source list so this is catalogued as a method only, not run.
themes: Expedia and Hotels.com datasets (Expedia hotel recommendation Kaggle, personalized ranking ICDM 2013, Expedia scrapers), Trivago RecSys 2019, Kayak/Skyscanner scrapers
Airline fare tracking datasets (Google Flights scrapers, Skyscanner, Hopper reports), airfare price indices
why_all: Another non-Airbnb, actively maintained flight-search puller relevant to gap 10 (airline capacity/traffic) and general travel-demand cross-checks; scraping Skyscanner is outside the sanctioned-source list so this is catalogued as a method only, not run.

Alternative live Skyscanner fare-acquisition method to Google Flights scrapers; only useful if the team decides to build and archive its own point-in-time airfare panel (a ToS question to flag per repo rules, since it scrapes a non-Airbnb but still commercial site).

name: thorwhalen/farepy
what_it_holds: Multi-source flight-search Python client with normalized results, caching, and batch support, including a Kayak integration alongside other flight-search backends.
why_useful: General-purpose flight-fare pull tool; could feed an airfare/travel-cost proxy series (gap #10) if a team member wants time-series airfare tracking beyond BLS/FRED airfare CPI already held, but it is a live scraper/aggregator client, not a stored dataset.
themes: Expedia and Hotels.com datasets (Expedia hotel recommendation Kaggle, personalized ranking ICDM 2013, Expedia scrapers), Trivago RecSys 2019, Kayak/Skyscanner scrapers

name: skyscanner/skyscanner-python-sdk
what_it_holds: Official (now archived/deprecated) Python SDK for the Skyscanner Flights, Hotels, and Car Hire APIs. Archived read-only Jan 2026; deprecated by Skyscanner itself since May 2020 with a stated warning the API will stop working. Apache License, 125 commits.
why_useful: Historical interest only -- confirms Skyscanner once exposed a hotel-price API wrapped here, but the underlying API is dead and the SDK is explicitly non-functional against current endpoints. Not a usable acquisition method today.
themes: Expedia and Hotels.com datasets (Expedia hotel recommendation Kaggle, personalized ranking ICDM 2013, Expedia scrapers), Trivago RecSys 2019, Kayak/Skyscanner scrapers
why_all: Historical interest only -- confirms Skyscanner once exposed a hotel-price API wrapped here, but the underlying API is dead and the SDK is explicitly non-functional against current endpoints. Not a usable acquisition method today.

name: ncl-cli
what_it_holds: Unofficial read-only CLI (MIT licence) that pulls Norwegian Cruise Line itinerary and shore-excursion data (plus images) from NCL's public site as JSON. No committed dataset — a live-pull method only. Updated 3 Jul 2026, 0 stars.
why_useful: Could be adapted to build a point-in-time itinerary/capacity-by-sailing panel for NCLH (gap #18, cruise book-ahead analogue) if run repeatedly and archived; on its own it is just a client, not data.
themes: Cruise line data: NCLH / Carnival / Royal Caribbean advance ticket sales, capacity, occupancy, cruise schedules and port calls
why_all: Could be adapted to build a point-in-time itinerary/capacity-by-sailing panel for NCLH (gap #18, cruise book-ahead analogue) if run repeatedly and archived; on its own it is just a client, not data.

name: Cruise_Tourism_Research_API_Request
what_it_holds: Uses the Google Maps API plus web-scripting tools to collect cruise ports and cruise ships data (port locations, ship metadata) for a tourism research project. Small academic project repo, MIT licence, last touched 2020, 1 star.
why_useful: A crude method sketch for building a port-call panel, but stale (2020), no committed output data visible, and Google Maps API is not a cruise-schedule source of real value.
themes: Cruise line data: NCLH / Carnival / Royal Caribbean advance ticket sales, capacity, occupancy, cruise schedules and port calls
